nar.text: It was decided to scrap the two P2's and use the stripped six-cylinder 1750 cc sports cars instead.
Varzi insists on racing the P2, with Ghersi as his reserve driver.
The single car start at Termini began at 9:00 in the morning in order of the starting numbers. The drivers were released at three minute intervals.
Varzi, in twelfth place with race number 30, took off nine minutes after Chiron and roared away in his typical emotionless, collected style.

Varzi came back from the first lap and sped past the grandstands after an unbelievable 1h21m21.6s at a speed of 49.492 mph, breaking Minoia's previous year's record lap of 1h25m17s at 47.215 mph by almost four minutes.
Nuvolari in second place was over one minute back, with Campari about half a minute behind. In fourth place followed Chiron.
Maggi retires three kilometres from the start; Balestrero's race ends in Polizzi.
Varzi's Alfa had a slight advantage over Chiron's Bugatti on the level coast road, while the Bugatti was superior in the mountains.
The hard driving Chiron had moved ahead of Campari and Nuvolari on elapsed time.
His second lap was almost identical to his first, only six seconds slower but faster than anyone else, increasing his advantage to Chiron to 3m18s.
Arcangeli's Maserati spins off with a locked brake and rolls over in a field before Polizzi; he retires.
Divo slides off after a fuel stop at Polizzi, smashing a wheel and bending the front stub axle.
The right stub axle was bent and he was forced to abandon the race at the end of lap two.
Varzi ended the second lap in 1h21m26.4s and stopped at the Cerda depot for tires and fuel which took only 1m18s.
Nuvolari stops at the pits to have a serious steering problem checked.
He needed 1h25m04.8s for the third tour and Chiron, with a fast lap of 1h23m38.2s, had reduced Varzi's advantage to two minutes.
Rough repaired road breaks Varzi's spare wheel mountings; he loses the spare and the fuel tank starts to leak.
Campari had to deal with gearbox problems when his car jumped out of third gear. As a result he was passed by Nuvolari.
He required 1h23m20.2s for his fourth lap, whereas Chiron did it in only 1h21m50.8s and had made up two minutes, lagging just 23 seconds behind Varzi.
At the end of lap four, Varzi darted into the pits to refuel and change all tires.
Williams collapses in the pits; Divo takes over his Bugatti for the last lap.
Ruggeri retires his O.M.
Varzi's pit stop to change tires and refuel at the end of lap four had cost him half a minute of his lead over Chiron. When he left the pits Chiron was leading on the clock.
Chiron's sick mechanic distracts him; the Bugatti hits a wall and breaks both left wheels, which they change by the roadside.
Varzi's leaking tank runs low; his mechanic refuels from a can on the move and the tail catches fire.
The mechanic began beating frantically at the flames with his seat cushion while the ice cold Varzi hunched down in his seat and drove as fast as possible downhill.
Varzi wins in 6h55m16.8s at 78.023 km/h; Chiron second, 1m48.8s behind.
Conelli had worked himself into third place ahead of Campari's delayed Alfa Romeo that kept jumping out of third gear.
Nuvolari, slowed with a broken front spring mounting, reached the finish almost ten minutes later.
Morandi passes Divo in Williams' Bugatti; then Maserati, d'Ippolito, Minoia, Borzacchini and Bittmann.
